title: Sports Entertainment Group Launches Adelaide Broadcast Precinct SEN SA House with AAMI Naming Rights
article_text:
Sports Entertainment Group (SEG) has announced a capital investment to establish SEN SA House, a state-of-the-art sports media and broadcast precinct at 1 King William Street on the corner of North Terrace in Adelaide’s central business district.

Announced on 16 November 2026 to mark SEN SA’s eighth anniversary, the development is backed by a three-year naming-rights partnership with Australian insurer AAMI. Scheduled for completion in late 2026, the facility sits within walking distance of Adelaide Oval and aims to more than double SEG’s locally produced audio, television, and digital content across South Australia.

Sports Entertainment group CEO, Craig Hutchison, highlighted the value of combining prime CBD visibility with expanded local news and television production.

“South Australia is one of the great sporting states, and over the past eight years we’ve been incredibly proud of what SEG has built here.”

“From day one, our focus has been on giving South Australian sports fans a genuine home for the teams, competitions and conversations they care about, delivered by people who know and love sport in this state.

“SEN SA House is the next step in that commitment.

“We want to create something special in the heart of Adelaide; a place where people can walk past and see their favourite broadcasters in action, where we can produce outstanding content, and where fans feel connected to the sports they love.

“We’re making a significant investment in local jobs, talent and content production, creating new opportunities for South Australians to work in sports media and giving fans even more locally produced coverage,” Hutchison said.

Suncorp executive general manager – brand and customer experience, Mim Haysom, underscored AAMI’s deepening commercial and community footprint within South Australian sport.

“South Australia is an important part of AAMI’s story, and we’re proud to continue building our presence and connections with communities across the state.”

“Sport has a special way of bringing South Australians together.

“Through our longstanding partnership with SANFL, and this new partnership with SEN SA House, we’re proud to support the sporting moments and experiences that matter to South Australians.

“We’re looking forward to seeing SEN SA House become a destination for sports fans and a vibrant addition to the heart of Adelaide,” Hayson said.

The expansion creates dozens of new full-time and part-time media roles, establishing a dedicated South Australian news service alongside expanded syndication agreements with Gold 1323 AM and regional network Flow FM across its 12 stations. Alongside AAMI—which houses its South Australian regional headquarters at the same 1 King William Street address, SEG secured commercial studio naming-rights agreements with home builder Metricon and national gym operator Revo Fitness to anchor its multi-platform production infrastructure.

AAMI Naming Rights & Broadcast Integration: Secures a three-year naming-rights agreement encompassing building façade signage, a purpose-built television production studio at 1 King William Street, and brand integration across local programming.

Metricon Street-Facing Radio Studio: Extends SEG’s partnership with Metricon through a two-year deal naming the street-facing Metricon Studio inside SEN SA House, serving as the live broadcast home for SEN SA’s breakfast programming.

Revo Fitness Podcast Studio: Establishes a dedicated audio production hub at SEG’s existing 2 King William Street headquarters, integrating Revo Fitness across locally produced podcast series.

title: Pro Climbing League raises £3.2m to expand after London sell-out
article_text:
The Pro Climbing League has raised £3.2m in seed funding to take independent professional climbing to more cities, after selling 4,000 tickets for its 2027 season on the first day.

Redrice Ventures led the round. Redrice counts Andy Murray and Alistair Brownlee as associate partners and was an early backer of British sportswear brand Castore. It was joined by Active Partners, London-based sports fund Accelerate Ventures and the International Bouldering Alliance, a European gym group. PCL describes the investment as one of the first times institutional capital has backed a climbing event or media brand outside the gym environment.

The funding will underpin a three-event season in 2027: Berlin on 23rd January 2027, Paris on 13th February 2027 and London on 20th March 2027. Five events are planned for 2028, including one in the US.

PCL’s London debut in February sold out in less than a day, with 2,500 seats available. In the women’s final, France’s Oriane Bertone beat double Olympic champion Janja Garnbret in front of more than 2,400 spectators. Some 43% of ticket buyers were female, and attendees came from 27 countries.

Danaan Markey, CEO of the Pro Climbing League, said, “We sold 4,000 tickets in the first day and are steadily climbing.”

Demand has led PCL to bring its expansion plans forward by a year and move to larger venues. The business earns revenue from tickets and sponsorship, with Red Bull, which broadcast the London event, as a major partner.

Prize money is central to the model. First place at major international events currently pays £6,000, while the London winners each took home £10,000. The prize pot will rise to £50,000 per event in 2027.

PCL was founded by Markey, a former German national team coach and Patagonia sports marketer, alongside climbing commentator Charlie Boscoe, former BBC Radio head of live events Neil Wyatt, and start-up operator Eelco Bulten.

Alistair Brownlee, Associate Partner at Redrice Ventures, said indoor climbing has grown from a subculture into a global phenomenon, pointing to mass participation, Olympic status and growing media recognition. He added that today’s climbers want to compete in and watch their sport, creating an audience with real commercial value.

title: Dana White's UFC fighter loan system faces scrutiny after RAF Abu Dhabi brawl arrests
article_text:
Dana White's UFC fighter loan system faces scrutiny following a series of violent incidents at Real American Freestyle wrestling events.

Merab Dvalishvili was involved in a fight by a group led by Usman Nurmagomedov in Abu Dhabi, resulting in 10 arrests and multiple convictions.

Usman Nurmagomedov's prospective UFC signing and his brother Umar's career prospects have been severely damaged by their six-month prison sentences.

The UFC has a history of tolerating pre-fight confrontations, with incidents involving Conor McGregor and others having become defining moments in the sport.

"It's crazy. I mean, they must like it for this to happen all the time," UFC president Dana White said of the recurring incidents.

Dana White has built a global sporting empire on the backs of fighters who are as adept at selling a fight outside the octagon as they are at winning one inside it.

But the UFC president may be discovering that when his stars step outside the organisation, the theatre of pre-fight promotion can spill over into something altogether more serious.

White has been happy to see some of his biggest names compete on Real American Freestyle (RAF) wrestling cards. But a series of ugly confrontations, culminating in last week's extraordinary scenes in Abu Dhabi, could force him to reconsider.

Initially, letting his MMA fighters compete on RAF wrestling cards made sense. There's no striking involved, so the risk of serious injuries and concussions is greatly reduced. It keeps athletes active in between fights and exposes them to a new audience.

To recap, Merab Dvalishvili, the former UFC bantamweight champion, was ambushed by a group led by fellow MMA fighter Usman Nurmagomedov in the lobby of the Yas Hilton hotel ahead of his appearance at RAF Abu Dhabi.

Police made 10 arrests. The Abu Dhabi Criminal Court subsequently convicted eight of those involved, with Dvalishvili and his accomplice, Saba Lazishvili, fined Dh50,000 each and released.

Footage of the attack went viral. Two of those convicted were jailed after publishing footage of the brawl.

It was bad for everyone involved, not least the Nurmagomedovs. Usman was in talks to sign with the UFC after becoming a free agent following the expiration of his PFL contract. Umar was already on the UFC roster. It is hard to see how either has a future in the organisation.

It followed another high-profile brawl involving two of White's star UFC names at the pre-fight press conference ahead of RAF 14 last month.

On that occasion, Arman Tsarukyan tried to get at Dillon Danis, a rent-a-gob jiu-jitsu practitioner who likes to antagonise his opponents with racial slurs and provocative statements.

Danis wore a T-shirt that depicted Khamzat Chimaev, another stud in the UFC stable who was sat in the front row, in a less than favourable light. A melee ensued before security got control of the situation.

That was spillover from Danis' loss to Chimaev at RAF 10. The UAE combat star pinned Danis in 44 seconds and kicked him up the backside as he lay on the mat after the referee's whistle, resulting in members of both teams storming the stage.

On Sunday, White was asked if the UFC was reconsidering loaning their fighters out to the RAF following a spate of incidents.

"It's crazy. I mean, they must like it for this to happen all the time," White said, shaking his head.

His frustration is understandable. A deal for Usman, the undefeated PFL lightweight champion and a genuine star, looks dead in the water. His brother Umar, a former world title contender at bantamweight, is unlikely to fight again until at least the back end of 2027, if he is retained at all.

Dvalishvili, the former UFC bantamweight champion, was lucky to suffer only cuts and bruises to his face following the attack. That he competed at RAF Abu Dhabi this past Saturday – and then called for Usman and his associates to be immediately released – is a testament to his character.

It's important to acknowledge that the UFC does RAF a favour in loaning out its fighters to compete against genuine world-class wrestlers and Olympians. It elevates RAF, something CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein acknowledges.

But from White's perspective, the CEO of a multibillion-dollar company doesn't want his fighters involved in violent altercations unless they are in the confines of a UFC octagon.

It also seems a bit rich that a man happy to let flames be fanned to sell a fight in his own organisation objects to it being done in others.

Fighters taking it to each other ahead of fights or at press conferences is nothing new, and certainly not in the UFC.

Conor McGregor specialised in it. Before his first fight with Nate Diaz in 2016, he and his camp exchanged insults and threw water bottles and cans at each other as the event descended into mayhem.

The Irishman and his entourage attacked a bus carrying Khabib Nurmagomedov – the trainer and cousin of Usman and Umar – and other fighters at Barclays Centre in Brooklyn ahead of UFC 299.

The incident left several fighters injured and became one of the defining moments in UFC history. The rivalry culminated in a post-fight brawl after Khabib submitted McGregor at UFC 229.

During a promotional press conference ahead of UFC 178, light-heavyweight rivals Jon Jones and Daniel Cormier went head-to-head before Jones shoved Cormier. Both fighters started swinging, knocking over the promotional backdrop and sending security scrambling.

title: Canadian insurance sponsorships are reshaping carrier brand strategy
article_text:
Canadian insurance sponsorships reached a new level of strategic intent in 2026, and the stakes for brokers are more concrete than they might appear. Carriers that do not distribute through independent brokers are using sports and community partnerships as their primary mechanism for building consumer familiarity – the kind of name recognition that broker relationships provide for other carriers organically. The broker question is not abstract: IBC’s own survey data shows the share of Canadian insurance clients who say they always rely fully on their broker’s recommendation to choose an insurer has fallen from 45% in 2024 to 35% in 2026. When clients arrive at a broker conversation having already formed a view of a carrier, that is partly a function of brand exposure. Sports sponsorship is one of the main ways carriers are creating that exposure.

The numbers frame the gap. According to the Canadian Life and Health Insurance Association’s (CLHIA) 2026 annual factbook, released October 20, 2026, 84% of life insurance in Canada – totalling $6.2 trillion in coverage across 23 million Canadians – is purchased through individual agents and advisors. Carriers that cannot access that channel must build consumer recognition another way. They are spending more doing so: according to the 2026 Canadian Sponsorship Landscape Study, released August 18, 2026, by T1 and the Sponsorship Marketing Council Canada, total sponsorship spending in Canada reached $4.7 billion – with brands planning to increase investment further.

Securian Canada’s activation at the 113th Grey Cup in November 2026 illustrates the approach. The Toronto-based insurer, which distributes creditor, group life, critical illness, and affinity products through banks, credit unions, and affinity groups rather than through independent brokers, has been the official life insurance partner of the Canadian Football League (CFL) since 2023. As part of that partnership, it also presents the CFL’s Diversity in Football programme, which provides career development pathways in professional football coaching and operations. For the 2026 Grey Cup, Securian Canada ran its second Game Changers contest – Kayla McNulty, a physical education teacher at Morin Heights Elementary School in Morin-Heights, Quebec, was selected from 381 nominations for launching her school’s first flag football programme. On November 15, 2026, she joined Securian Canada to present the Most Valuable Player award in Calgary.

“The people who make the greatest difference in our communities don’t always seek recognition. They’re the ones who see potential where others see barriers,” Nigel Branker, chief executive officer of Securian Canada in Toronto, said in the company’s November 12, 2026, press release.

The programme is in its second year. Its inaugural 2025 winner, James Dickens, was recognised for more than 18 years as a firefighter, coaching youth football, and more than 22 years of military service. Securian Canada’s 2025 Beyond Business Report records that Dickens was nominated while navigating treatment for stage-four cancer, attended the Grey Cup in Winnipeg with his partner, and passed away in December 2025.

Securian Canada is not the only carrier using sport as a consumer brand channel. Allstate Canada, which distributes through its exclusive captive agent network, extended its official insurance partnership with Canada Soccer and the Canadian Premier League through 2030, confirmed in June 2026. Like Securian Canada, its sports investment functions primarily as a direct-to-consumer visibility play.

Beneva, Canada’s largest mutual insurer, distributes through brokers and advisors outside Quebec – a commitment it reaffirmed as part of its January 2026 merger with Gore Mutual. It has nonetheless been building a national portfolio of running event title sponsorships since its 2020 formation, with the Calgary Marathon announced in September 2026 becoming its seventh running event in Canada, as IBC’s coverage of Beneva’s growing national running sponsorship strategy across Canadian cities has documented. Intact Insurance, which distributes through both independent brokers via its Intact brand and directly through belairdirect, became the national partner of the Canadian Olympic Committee in October 2025, running through the 2028 Los Angeles Summer Games.

For broker-distributed carriers, sports partnerships serve a different purpose than they do for non-broker carriers. Consumer-facing brand investment can reinforce the value of the broker relationship – a client who arrives already recognising a carrier name requires less education at the point of advice. That is the more benign reading. The less comfortable reading, supported by the decline in full broker reliance noted above, is that carriers building direct consumer familiarity through sport are quietly shifting the dynamics of the advice conversation before a client ever reaches a broker.

Brokerages have increasingly entered the sports sponsorship market in response. Western Financial Group, one of Canada’s largest national insurance brokerages, entered a multi-year CFL jersey sponsorship with the Winnipeg Blue Bombers in February 2026, following a similar deal with the Calgary Stampeders that established its western Canadian brand presence through sport. HUB International signed a multi-year deal as the official employee benefits partner of the Professional Women’s Hockey League (PWHL) in Canada, covering five Canadian markets from the 2026-27 season. Navacord partnered with the Toronto Maple Leafs, and Acera Insurance and Navacord jointly signed a deal with Vancouver Whitecaps FC through the 2027-28 season.

For brokerages, the aim is national brand credibility – differentiating on something other than price or product access in a market where the Insurance Brokers Association of Canada’s Broker Identity Program attracted renewal commitments from more than a dozen carriers in 2026, funding advertising and advocacy on the broker channel’s behalf. For independent brokers, the practical implication is direct: when both non-broker carriers and large consolidator brokerages are investing in consumer recognition through sport, the independent broker’s most defensible position is the advice relationship itself. Brokers and agents held 58% of the Canadian P&C market as of 2025, according to the Custom Market Insights Canada Property & Casualty Insurance Market report. That majority rests on the value of advice – and the sponsorship investments of carriers that do not use brokers are, in effect, a bet that consumer familiarity can begin to substitute for it.

title: News: NHL media rights, Paramount-WBD, Angels and more
article_text:
The NHL has reportedly approached ESPN and TNT Sports about media rights renewals; Paramount has updated aspects of its hostile tender offer for Warner Bros. Discovery; and in-market streaming of Los Angeles Angels broadcasts will take place through the MLB DTC platform. Plus news on ESPN, Netflix, CBS-UFC and Fubo.

NHL commissioner Gary Bettman is said to have approached ESPN and TNT Sports about expediting their media rights negotiations, according to John Ourand of Puck Tuesday night. Ourand, who reported the same about the PGA Tour, wrote that the networks do not appear poised to negotiate new deals “until they know how much the NFL will ask for.” The NFL currently receives a reported sum of more than $11 billion annually for its media rights.

The NHL’s U.S. media rights deals, which are reportedly worth a combined $625 million, are not due to expire until after the 2028 season. But with the NFL widely expected to move up its media rights negotiations, leagues are reportedly looking to rush to the negotiating table while the networks still have money to spend.

TNT Sports lost its domestic NBA media rights package last year, but has in recent years acquired French Open tennis, NASCAR and — via sublicense — College Football Playoff games, among other properties. ESPN has committed billions in new rights and renewals since reacquiring NHL rights in March 2021 after a 17-year hiatus.

The NHL last year signed a 12-year media rights extension with Rogers Communications in Canada worth $11 billion CDN, but it does not begin until the 2026-27 season. Between the United States and Canada, the league will bring in reported media revenue of more than $1.2 billion USD per year for the two seasons those deals overlap.

Paramount on Tuesday updated its hostile tender offer for all of Warner Bros. Discovery to cover the $2.8 billion termination fee WBD would need to pay to get out of its commitment with Netflix, and add a $0.25/share “ticking fee” to WBD shareholders for every quarter the deal is not closed. The latter equates to approximately $650 million in cash value that would be distributed among WBD shareholders per quarter. Paramount again expressed confidence in quickly receiving the necessary regulatory approvals for the proposed transaction, which the company first initiated with a series of unsolicited bids starting last fall.

Paramount had previously sweetened its deal by raising the reverse termination fee to $5.8 billion, which is equivalent to the Netflix figure. Either of these suitors would need to compensate WBD with this fee if their pact does not receive regulatory approval. In its “enhanced” tender offer, Paramount claimed it would “fully reimburse” WBD for the potential $1.5 billion cost affiliated with not completing debt refinancing. The company said this payment would not reduce the reverse termination fee.

Paramount, which extended the expiration date for its offer by 10 days to March 2, has secured $43.6 billion in equity commitments coming from both the Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners, including an “irrevocable personal guarantee” from Larry Ellison. Paramount also has $54 billion in debt commitments from Apollo, Bank of America and Citigroup. Moreover, Paramount said its financing sources would extend the maturity on a $15 billion bridge loan or that the company would “permit WBD to structure permanent financing in any way it chooses so long as the debt is redeemable at a commercially reasonable cost.”

Paramount has continued to argue that its bid is “superior” to the Netflix agreement, claiming the latter is operating off a sliding scale based on the amount of debt to be carried by Discovery Global. WBD disclosed that Discovery Global would carry $17 billion of debt “as of June 30, 2026” with a goal to reduce that number to $16.1 billion by year’s end. Since WBD is able to determine the amount of debt Discovery will hold prior to pro rata common stock distribution, a “debt adjustment mechanism” in the Netflix deal could potentially reduce its value. WBD confirmed receipt of Paramount’s offer, which its board will review.

The Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday joined the list of 21 Major League Baseball teams whose games will be distributed digitally via the league’s in-house direct-to-consumer platform, but it remains to be seen whether the team’s games will be produced by the league. The Angels are co-owners of the FanDuel Sports Network West RSN and are “contemplating buying out Main Street to launch their own network,” per a report by Mike Mazzeo of Sports Business Journal. Mazzeo cited sources who explained that the team has not ruled out launching a linear network this season or in the future, which could also include Los Angeles Kings NHL games.

While the majority of teams are working with MLB on the distribution of their games, not all of them are utilizing the league for production. At the moment, MLB is slated to produce live game broadcasts for the five teams it worked with last season (Diamondbacks, Guardians, Rockies, Twins, Padres) in addition to eight teams previously part of the Main Street Sports Group portfolio (Reds, Tigers, Royals, Marlins, Brewers, Cardinals, Rays, Nationals). The Seattle Mariners organization is also working with the league on production and distribution of local games after shutting down ROOT Sports Northwest last year.

For the 14 teams whose games are being both produced and distributed by MLB, the in-market streaming price is $20/month and $100 for the season. While the Angels have not announced their production arrangements for the upcoming season, the pricing is the same. MLB is also distributing local games televised on RSNs for six teams this season as well (Athletics, Orioles, Dodgers, Mets, Phillies, Giants). The pricing for these packages differs by market, and some of the solutions also include access to other programming from the applicable RSN.

title: $13 million deal brings new name to Pan American Center - Las Cruces Sun-News
article_text:
A 10-year, $13 million naming rights agreement will turn the Pan American Center into White Sands Federal Credit Union Arena at the Pan American Center.

The agreement will run through the 2035-36 academic year, according to an announcement from New Mexico State University on Friday, Nov. 13. It is the first naming rights agreement in the nearly 58-year history of the NMSU venue, which opened Nov. 30, 1968.

White Sands Federal Credit Union secured the naming rights through a partnership involving the university athletic department and Van Wagner. The arena is home to the Aggies’ men’s basketball, women’s basketball and volleyball programs.

Revenue from the agreement will support efforts to improve the student-athlete experience and help fund the athletic department's 16 NCAA Division I programs, according to the announcement.

The Pan American Center also hosts concerts, commencement ceremonies, community gatherings and other entertainment events.

“This is a landmark moment in the history of New Mexico State University Athletics, and I want to express my sincere appreciation to White Sands Federal Credit Union for their partnership and investment in our future,” athletic director Joe Fields said in the release. “Their commitment to the Pan American Center demonstrates tremendous confidence in NMSU and the Southern New Mexico region. Partnerships like this elevate our university, strengthen our connection with the community, and position us to continue building a first-class athletics department.”

White Sands Federal Credit Union said the agreement reflects the credit union’s shared ties with New Mexico State University and Southern New Mexico.

“This partnership represents much more than placing our name on the Pan American Center; it is an investment in our region, our students, and the communities we serve,” a statement attributed to the credit union said in the release. “We look forward to building meaningful relationships, creating new opportunities, and making a lasting positive impact throughout Southern New Mexico for generations to come.”

The Van Wagner Group works in sports advertising, multimedia rights and live event production. Its services include sponsorship and media sales, collegiate multimedia rights, advertising and broadcast production.

title: Iraq grapples with federation mess and uncertainty over Graham Arnold's future
article_text:
Iraqi football is in disarray. Its federation is consumed by feuds, legal challenges and accusations of political meddling. And now Graham Arnold, the Australian coach who ended the country’s 40-year wait for a World Cup, may be about to take charge of his last match.

Iraqi media report that his successor will be Emad Mohammed, a former national team striker with a patchy record in the dugout.

The Iraqi Football Association is governed by a president chosen by 61 voting delegates drawn from clubs, regional bodies and professional associations. In Iraq, the job brings money, influence and political prestige. So, inevitably, parties and powerful benefactors take an interest in who gets it.

For five years, that man was Adnan Dirjal, a defender from the generation that qualified for the 1986 World Cup and a former sports minister. His deputy was Younis Mahmoud, the revered captain who lifted the 2007 Asian Cup.

The partnership’s collapse played out in public. In 2023, Mahmoud told a television audience that he had tried to curb Dirjal’s authority over contracts relating to the staging of the 2023 Gulf Cup that had been signed without the board’s knowledge. In August 2025, Mahmoud announced that he would stand against him.

World Cup qualification should have made Dirjal untouchable, but Mahmoud prevailed in May by 38 votes to 20, just before the tournament kicked off.

Dirjal stormed out, sarcastically congratulating the politician Mohammed Al Halbousi and Olympic Committee president Aqeel Muftin, both of whom he accused of orchestrating his defeat. Mahmoud’s camp denied any interference, and the Court of Arbitration for Sport has twice refused Dirjal’s requests to suspend the new board pending a final ruling on his challenge to the election.

One of the players who credited Dirjal for his work was Ali Al Hamadi. In an interview with The National, before the World Cup, the striker was asked whether a dressing room which included Kurds, Arabs, Chaldeans and Assyrians, in a country long scarred by division, ever discussed politics.

His response: “I think this is definitely probably the most together it’s ever been. And that’s credit to the staff, that’s credit to Adnan Dirjal as well for his work behind the scenes, recruiting players, the organisation.”

Arnold was Dirjal’s appointment, and the new leadership inherited him weeks before the World Cup. Despite Iraq losing all three of their World Cup matches, Arnold was offered a four-year contract in July but agreed to sign for six months instead, intended to take him through to the 2027 Asian Cup.

He reasoned that a long deal might cost him his passion for the job and leave the federation with an expensive payout. However, the federation's vice-president, Sarmad Abdulilah, subsequently acknowledged that Arnold had also raised serious concerns about administrative failings, including arrangements for training camps, player transport and communications with clubs.

The new leadership began to introduce their own changes. The team’s manager, Mustafa Jalal, was replaced by Dr Mushtaq Kadhim, whose father has long-standing ties to Al Naft, an oil-backed club with a vote in federation elections. Jalal was experienced, fluent in English and was said to have worked well with Arnold’s foreign staff.

On the pitch, Iraq’s results were fuelling criticism. At the Gulf Cup in September, they needed only a draw against an already-qualified Saudi Arabia, but Arnold made changes due to concerns that players already on yellow cards could miss the semi-finals. His side lost 2-0.

But the federation stood by him, publicly reaffirming their confidence in the Australian in October.

Then earlier this month, the Asian Cup was postponed over security threats in Saudi Arabia. Arnold’s contract expires in February, leaving him without the tournament he had stayed on to coach.

Emad is widely tipped to be Arnold’s successor. In July, Mahmoud reportedly told him he would be first choice should talks with Arnold collapse.

On paper, he ticks a few boxes. Born in Kerbala in 1982, he was a striker who won 103 caps and scored 27 goals for Iraq. As a coach, he guided Iraq’s Under-20 side to the final of the 2023 Asian Championship and on to the World Cup in Argentina.

But is he the best candidate? His spells in club football were brief. His Under-23 team exited the 2026 Asian Championship without a victory, after which he said the federation had talked him out of resigning.

In 2024, Fifa banned him for six months over insults aimed at a television presenter, though he denied responsibility for the social media account involved. What makes it all the more interesting is that Emad himself noted in July that Arnold should stay and finish what he started.

At the weekend, Iraqi media reported that Tuesday's match against Iran in Basra would be Arnold's last, regardless of the result. Federation sources claimed the board had agreed he would not continue, although no replacement had been confirmed. Emad is reportedly willing to take over if offered a long-term contract.

Importantly, Mahmoud also recently revealed that the federation was facing a financial crisis with a monthly wage bill of more than 400 million Iraqi dinars for national team coaches and their staff.

But the federation has yet to confirm any decision. Mahmoud said the coach's future would be discussed only when the senior and Olympic teams had finished their current matches, while board member Ghalib Al Zamili insisted the Australian will continue under his current contract.

title: Alzheimer’s Research UK becomes World Seniors Snooker charity partner
article_text:
Alzheimer’s Research UK has joined the World Seniors Snooker Tour as its charity partner, bringing the sport’s most recognisable veteran names behind the push for a cure for dementia.

The partnership will raise awareness of dementia and the need for research, while creating opportunities to generate funds for the charity’s work. The Tour will use its events, platforms and profile within the sport to spotlight Alzheimer’s Research UK and encourage players, fans and supporters to back the cause.

Alzheimer’s Research UK is the largest UK charity dedicated to dementia research. It funds research, challenges misconceptions and supports everyone affected by a condition that touches millions of families across the country.

Rohit Sagoo, Director at the World Seniors Snooker Tour, said, “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Alzheimer’s Research UK as our official charity partner. Dementia is a cause that touches so many people and families, and we are proud to be able to use the platform of the World Seniors Snooker Tour to help raise awareness and support the incredible work being undertaken by Alzheimer’s Research UK.“

“Snooker is a sport that brings generations together, and we hope this partnership will allow us to make a meaningful contribution to a cause that deserves all the support it can get.”

The partnership also ties into the charity’s Think Brain Health campaign, which sets out three simple rules to help reduce dementia risk: love your heart, stay sharp and keep connected.

Zoe Dean, Senior Relationship Fundraiser at Alzheimer’s Research UK, said, “We are delighted to be the official charity partner for the World Seniors Snooker Tour. Snooker has such a passionate and engaged community, and this partnership gives us a fantastic opportunity to raise awareness of dementia, inspire people to get involved and raise vital funds for research. Playing snooker is also a great way to stay sharp and keep connected, two key messages of our Think Brain Health campaign that encourages people to take positive steps to look after their brain health.“

Alzheimer’s Society sponsored Talent Campaign of the Year at the 2026 SIAs and is an official partner and category partner again for the 2027 SIAs.

title: Galo announces Sólides sponsorship for the Copa Sul-Americana final
article_text:
Atlético will have Sólides as a one-match sponsor for the CONMEBOL Sudamericana final. The Minas Gerais-based company will have its brand displayed on the side hem of the black-and-white shirt for the clash against Argentina's Boca Juniors, scheduled for November 21 at 7:30 p.m. (Brasília time) at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Meléndez in Barranquilla, Colombia.

The partnership reinforces the presence of Minas Gerais companies alongside Atlético at an important moment in the club's international journey. "We are pleased and proud to display the brand of a company founded in Minas Gerais, but with a strong national presence, in Galo's most important match of the year. This Sólides sponsorship reinforces the club's commitment to always seeking opportunities to find partners who share our vision for the club's future," says Márcio Freire, Atlético's Vice President of Business.

Sólides' Marketing Director, Rafael Kahane, also welcomes the partnership. "As a company founded in Minas Gerais and now Brazil's leader in people management for SMEs, supporting Atlético in this Copa Sudamericana final is a source of immense pride. Having our brand on Galo's shirt in what promises to be a historic clash symbolizes the strength and presence of Minas Gerais on the international stage. We stand alongside the club and its fans to take our state's name even further."

In addition to brand exposure on the team's kit, the agreement includes other activation initiatives, such as producing promotional videos featuring Galo Doido and a first-team player. There are also plans to make Profiler, a behavioral mapping and analysis tool developed by Sólides, available to Atlético's club members.

The growing relationship between the organizations also includes initiatives related to management and leadership development. Last month, Mônica Hauck, CEO and co-founder of Sólides, attended a meeting at Arena MRV with members of Atlético's board and CEO Pedro Daniel as part of the club's leadership development program.

During the session, the executive shared her experience and insights on people management, organizational culture, innovation, and high performance. Organized by Atlético's HR department, the meeting is part of a series of exchanges with business executives aimed at improving decision-making and preparing the club's professionals for the challenges of football.

Sólides is a technology company and Brazil's leader in people management for small and medium-sized businesses. The company offers innovative solutions and proprietary methodologies that help attract, develop, and retain talent—reducing employee turnover and increasing businesses' competitive advantages. The company received the largest investment ever made in an HR tech company in Latin America, R$530 million, and strengthened its growth through strategic acquisitions of solutions focused on automating personnel administration and people management processes, expanding its portfolio and establishing itself as a one-stop shop for SMEs. It currently has more than 55,000 clients, with its platform impacting over 27 million lives, and stands out as a leader among Brazil's high-growth companies.

title: Flamengo revisits main sponsorship and could post a bigger-than-expected loss
Defending champs TKR secure boost for CPL as bpTT steps up
article_text:
Five-time champions and defending titleholders Trinbago Knight Riders (TKR) have secured major backing for the upcoming Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) season, officially locking in bp Trinidad and Tobago (bpTT) as a key sponsor.

The historic partnership was sealed on Tuesday at a signing ceremony at the Hyatt Regency, Port-of-Spain, marking the energy giant’s first-ever national-level sports sponsorship of this scale.

TKR enter the 2026 campaign riding high as the CPL's most successful franchise, aiming to add a sixth star to their chest. The alliance with bpTT brings powerful local backing to the team as they prepare to battle the region’s best on cricket’s biggest regional stage.

"bpTT is committed to supporting sport, culture and national pride in T&T," said David Campbell, President of bp Latin America and the Caribbean. "We are honoured to come on board as a sponsor of the Trinbago Knight Riders. TKR’s success is based on dedication and a commitment to excellence–qualities that align to our values at bp. We are looking forward to accompanying TKR on their journey to defend their CPL title."

For bpTT, the deal marks a bold expansion of its sports investment strategy. The sponsorship builds on bpTT’s long-standing support for sport, particularly in their fenceline community of Mayaro and Guayaguayare, and represents an expansion of that commitment to a wider national platform.

Coinciding with bpTT’s 65th anniversary of operations in Trinidad and Tobago, company representatives noted that partnering with TKR reflects six and a half decades of shared values, passion, and national pride.

With the 2026 CPL season fast approaching, the defending champions now have the backing of one of the country's biggest corporate giants as they set their sights on back-to-back glory.
